steps.scene: Squeezing past in a narrow street, you clip another car's wing mirror. Nobody seems to have noticed.

options.text: Drive on — it's only minor damage
Come back later and leave a note

question.explanation: If you're involved in a collision that causes damage or injury, you must stop. It doesn't matter how small it is.

steps.title: After a collision
steps.body: Give your name, address and registration number to anyone who reasonably asks. If you can't, report it to the police within 24 hours.

question.prompt: What should you share after a collision that damages another car?

options.text: Your name, address and vehicle registration number
Nothing, if the police aren't called

question.explanation: The other driver needs to know who you are and which vehicle was involved. Note their details too.

steps.title: First at a crash
steps.prompt: You're first to arrive at a crash on a busy road. Put what you do in order.

items.text: Warn other traffic — switch on your hazard lights
Get engines switched off and make sure no one smokes
Help the injured, without moving them unless you must

steps.explanation: Stop the crash getting worse first, then get help coming, then look after the people.

steps.scene: You've broken down on an ordinary two-way road. There's a warning triangle in the boot.

question.prompt: How far behind the car should you put it?

options.text: Right behind the car, where it's easy to see

question.explanation: 45 metres gives drivers time to react. Never use a warning triangle on a motorway.

steps.scene: Your car breaks down in a long road tunnel.

options.text: Stay in the car with the doors locked until help arrives
Keep trying to restart it until it goes
Switch on your hazard lights, then go and call for help

question.explanation: A stopped car in a tunnel is a serious danger. Use the emergency point to call for help straight away.

a.label: Fire, and you can drive
a.body: Drive the car out of the tunnel if you can do it safely.

b.label: Fire, and you can't
b.body: Pull over, switch off, get everyone out and go to an emergency point.

question.prompt: Your car catches fire in a tunnel. What should you do?

options.text: Drive it out of the tunnel if it's safe to do so
Open the bonnet to find the fire

question.explanation: The biggest danger in a tunnel is smoke. Getting the car out, if you safely can, keeps it out of everyone's air.

steps.wrongBelief: A smell of fuel from your car is normal and nothing to worry about.

question.prompt: You notice a strong smell of fuel while you're driving. What should you do?

options.text: Carry on and fill up at the next garage
Stop safely and find out where it's coming from
Open the windows and keep driving

question.explanation: Leaking fuel is a serious fire risk. Get it checked before you go on.

steps.repairNote: A strong fuel smell can mean a leak and a fire risk. Stop safely and check it out.
